## Problem 1

### Part a
```{r}
# Read data
data1 <- read_xpt("data/AUX_I.xpt")
data2 <- read_xpt("data/DEMO_I.xpt")

# Merge dataframes
df <- merge(data1, data2, by = "SEQN")
# Dimensions
dim(df)
```
### Part b
```{r}
# Cleaning columns
# Gender
df$RIAGENDR <- factor(df$RIAGENDR,
                      levels = c(1, 2),
                      labels = c("Male", "Female"))
# Citizenship
df$DMDCITZN[df$DMDCITZN != 1 & df$DMDCITZN != 2] <- NA
df$DMDCITZN <- factor(df$DMDCITZN,
                      levels = c(1, 2),
                      labels = c("Citizen", "Noncitizen"))
# Number of children <= 5 y.o. - no missing values

# Household income
df$INDHHIN2[df$INDHHIN2 == 77 | df$INDHHIN2 == 99] <- NA
df$INDHHIN2 <- factor(df$INDHHIN2,
                      levels = c(1:10, 12:15),
                      labels = c("$0-$4,999", "$5,000-$9,999", "$10,000-$14,999", "$15,000-$19,999", "$20,000-$24,999", "$25,000-$34,999", "$35,000-$44,999", "$45,000-$54,999", "$55,000-$64,999", "$65,000-$74,999", ">=$20,000", "<$20,000", "$75,000-$99,999", ">=$100,000"))
# Fix order as continuous
df$INDHHIN2 <- as.numeric(factor(df$INDHHIN2,
                      levels = c("$0-$4,999", "$5,000-$9,999", "$10,000-$14,999", "$15,000-$19,999", "<$20,000", ">=$20,000", "$20,000-$24,999", "$25,000-$34,999", "$35,000-$44,999", "$45,000-$54,999", "$55,000-$64,999", "$65,000-$74,999", "$75,000-$99,999", ">=$100,000")))
```

### Part c
```{r}
# Fit models
model1 <- glm(AUXTWIDR ~ RIAGENDR, data = df, family = poisson)
model2 <- glm(AUXTWIDR ~ RIAGENDR + DMDCITZN + DMDHHSZA + INDHHIN2, data = df, family = poisson)
model3 <- glm(AUXTWIDL ~ RIAGENDR, data = df, family = poisson)
model4 <- glm(AUXTWIDL ~ RIAGENDR + DMDCITZN + DMDHHSZA + INDHHIN2, data = df, family = poisson)
```

```{r}
models <- list(model1, model2, model3, model4)
# Extract IRR of coefficients
irr <- sapply(models, function(x) {round(exp(coef(x)), digits = 2)})
names(irr) <- c("model1", "model2", "model3", "model4")
irr.df <- data.frame(lapply(irr, function(x) {
  length(x) <- max(lengths(irr))
  return(x)
}))
# Print table
kable(irr.df, row.names = TRUE, caption = "IRR of Coefficients in each model")

# Extract Statistics
sizes <- sapply(models, nobs)
psuedo_R2 <- sapply(models, function(x){round(pR2(x), digits = 5)})["McFadden",]
AICs <- sapply(models, function(x){round(AIC(x), digits = 1)})

# Print table
stat_table <- data.frame(rbind(model = c("model1", "model2", "model3", "model4"), sizes = sizes, psuedo_R2 = psuedo_R2, AICs = AICs))
kable(stat_table)
```

### Part d
```{r}
# Check p-value of coefficient
print(summary(model4))
# Predicted marginal means
emm <- emmeans(model4, ~ RIAGENDR, type = "response")
contrast(emm, method = "pairwise", type = "response")
```
:::{.callout-tip icon="false"}
## Answer
The p-value associated with the gender coefficient is less than 0.05, which is evidence for a difference between males and females in terms of IRR. The p-value associated with the difference of predicted value between males is also less than 0.05, suggesting the difference is significant.
:::

## Problem 2
```{r}
sakila <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "data/sakila_master.db")
```

### Part a
```{r}
# Extract table
dbGetQuery(sakila, "
SELECT store_id, active
  FROM Customer
") |> 
# Calculate statistics
  group_by(store_id) |> 
  summarize(
    n_cust = n(),
    active_per = round(mean(as.numeric(active)), 2)
  )

# SQL query
dbGetQuery(sakila, "
SELECT store_id, Count(active) AS n_cust, Round(Avg(active),2) AS active_per
  FROM Customer
  GROUP BY store_id
")

```

```{r}
# calculate runtime
microbenchmark(
R = dbGetQuery(sakila, "
SELECT store_id, active
  FROM Customer
") |> 
  group_by(store_id) |> 
  summarize(
    n_cust = n(),
    active_per = round(mean(as.numeric(active)), 2)
  ) ,
SQL = dbGetQuery(sakila, "
SELECT store_id, Count(active) AS n_cust, Round(Avg(active),2) AS active_per
  FROM Customer
  GROUP BY store_id
")
)
```

### Part b
```{r}
# Extract tables
staff <- dbGetQuery(sakila, "
SELECT first_name, last_name, address_id
  FROM staff
")
address <- dbGetQuery(sakila, "
SELECT address_id, city_id
  FROM address
")
city <- dbGetQuery(sakila, "
SELECT city_id, country_id
  FROM city
")
country <- dbGetQuery(sakila, "
SELECT country_id, country
  FROM country
")

# Merge tables and extract columns
staff |> 
  inner_join(address, by = "address_id") |> 
  inner_join(city, by = "city_id") |> 
  inner_join(country, by = "country_id") |> 
  select(first_name, last_name, country)

# SQL query
dbGetQuery(sakila, "
SELECT first_name, last_name, country
  FROM staff
    INNER JOIN address ON staff.address_id = address.address_id
    INNER JOIN city ON address.city_id = city.city_id
    INNER JOIN country ON city.country_id = country.country_id
")
```

```{r}
# calculate runtime
microbenchmark(
R = {staff <- dbGetQuery(sakila, "
```

### Part c
```{r}
# Extract tables
film <- dbGetQuery(sakila, "
  SELECT title, film_id
    FROM film
  ")
inventory <- dbGetQuery(sakila, "
  SELECT film_id, inventory_id
    FROM inventory
  ")
rental <-dbGetQuery(sakila, "
  SELECT inventory_id, rental_id
    FROM rental
  ")
payment <- dbGetQuery(sakila, "
  SELECT rental_id, amount
    FROM payment
  ")
# Merge tables and calculate maxima
film |> 
  inner_join(inventory, by = "film_id") |> 
  inner_join(rental, by = "inventory_id") |> 
  inner_join(payment, by = "rental_id") |> 
  select(title, amount) |> 
  group_by(title) |> 
  summarize(max_title = max(amount)) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  filter(max_title == max(max_title))

# SQL query
dbGetQuery(sakila, "
WITH FilmsMaxRent AS (SELECT title, max(amount) AS max_film
        FROM film
          INNER JOIN inventory ON film.film_id = inventory.film_id
          INNER JOIN rental ON inventory.inventory_id = rental.inventory_id
          INNER JOIN payment ON rental.rental_id = payment.rental_id
        GROUP BY title)
SELECT title, max_film 
  FROM FilmsMaxRent
  WHERE max_film = (SELECT max(max_film) from FilmsMaxRent)
")
```

```{r}
# Calculate runtimes
microbenchmark(
R = {film <- dbGetQuery(sakila, "
  SELECT title, film_id
    FROM film
  ")
  inventory <- dbGetQuery(sakila, "
    SELECT film_id, inventory_id
      FROM inventory
    ")
  rental <-dbGetQuery(sakila, "
    SELECT inventory_id, rental_id
      FROM rental
    ")
  payment <- dbGetQuery(sakila, "
    SELECT rental_id, amount
      FROM payment
    ")
  film |> 
    inner_join(inventory, by = "film_id") |> 
    inner_join(rental, by = "inventory_id") |> 
    inner_join(payment, by = "rental_id") |> 
    select(title, amount) |> 
    group_by(title) |> 
    summarize(max_title = max(amount)) |> 
    ungroup() |> 
    filter(max_title == max(max_title))},
SQL = dbGetQuery(sakila, "
  WITH FilmsMaxRent AS (SELECT title, max(amount) AS max_film
        FROM film
          INNER JOIN inventory ON film.film_id = inventory.film_id
          INNER JOIN rental ON inventory.inventory_id = rental.inventory_id
          INNER JOIN payment ON rental.rental_id = payment.rental_id
        GROUP BY title)
  SELECT title, max_film 
    FROM FilmsMaxRent
    WHERE max_film = (SELECT max(max_film) from FilmsMaxRent)
  ")
)
```

## Problem 3

```{r}
data <- read.csv("data/au-500.csv")
```

### Part a
```{r}
websites <- data$web
n_match <- length(grep("\\.com$", websites))
total <- length(websites)
paste0("The percentage of websites ending in '.com' is: ", n_match/total*100, "%.")
```

### Part b
```{r}
pattern <- "@[A-Za-z.]+\\.[A-Za-z]+$"
emails <- data$email
domains <- regmatches(emails, regexpr(pattern, emails))
table(domains)[which.max(table(domains))]
```
### Part c
```{r}
pattern <- "[^A-Za-z, ]"
companies <- data$company_name
matches <- grep(pattern, companies)
paste("The proportion of companies with a non-alphabetical, non-comma, or non-space character in the name is:", length(matches)/length(companies))

pattern2 <- "[^A-Za-z,& ]" 
matches2 <- grep(pattern2, companies)
paste("The proportion of companies with a non-alphabetical, non-comma, non-ampersand, or non-space character in the name is:", length(matches2)/length(companies))
```

### Part d
```{r}
#column 1
numbers <- data$phone1
digits <- gsub("-", "", numbers)
data$phone1 <- gsub("([0-9]{4})([0-9]{3})([0-9]{3})", "\\1-\\2-\\3", digits)
head(data$phone1, 10)

# column 2
numbers <- data$phone2
digits <- gsub("-", "", numbers)
data$phone2 <- gsub("([0-9]{4})([0-9]{3})([0-9]{3})", "\\1-\\2-\\3", digits)
head(data$phone2, 10)
```

### Part e
```{r}
pattern <- "[0-9]+$"
addresses <- data$address
apt_nums <- as.numeric(regmatches(addresses, regexpr(pattern, addresses)))
hist(log(apt_nums))
```

### Part f
```{r}
first_dig <- as.numeric(substr(as.character(apt_nums), 1, 1))
length(first_dig[first_dig == 1])/length(first_dig)
length(first_dig[first_dig == 9])/length(first_dig)
```
:::{.callout-tip icon="false"}
## Answer
The data do not appear to follow Bedford's law, since the percentage of numbers with 1 as the first digit is 9.2% and the percentage of numbers with 9 as the first digit is 14.6% instead of 30% and 5% respectively. This means the data would likely not be considered real.
:::
